mainTopic: Did בית שמאי act on their view about צרות, and did the two schools warn each other? Also רבי אלעזר's rule that a ממזר comes only from a union of ערוה with כרת
overview: The גמרא finishes a proof from the laws of טהרות that בית שמאי and בית הלל told each other when something was a problem in the other's view. It explains that this proof was needed because a צרה marriage might be so well known that no warning would be given. It then turns to רבי אלעזר's statement that both schools agree a ממזר comes only from a union of ערוה punishable by כרת. Its point is to reject רבי עקיבא, who holds that a union forbidden only by a לאו also produces a ממזר. Next the גמרא brings a ברייתא: despite many disputes about marriage and divorce, the two schools still married each other, out of love and friendship. From רבי שמעון's words, that they held back only in certain cases, the גמרא proves that בית שמאי acted on their view. It explains that for בית שמאי the holding back was about the צרה herself. It then rereads רבי שמעון's word 'doubtful' as 'unspecified': since the schools warned each other, silence meant there was no problem. Finally it begins a new proof from רבי יוחנן בן נורי, who sees a problem in following either school and starts to propose an enactment for the צרות; his words continue on the next amud.

steps.title: Proof from purity: if they were not told, בית שמאי could still use בית הלל's items
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sets up a proof from טהרות. If they told each other, it makes sense that neither group avoided the other's items. If they did not tell each other, at least בית שמאי had no reason to avoid בית הלל's items, since בית הלל is the stricter side here.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well if you say they told each other: that is why they did not avoid each other's items. But if you say they did not tell each other, it still makes sense that בית שמאי did not avoid בית הלל's items, because what בית הלל calls impure, בית שמאי calls pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a proof that בית שמאי and בית הלל warned each other. Here it checks the side of the story that works with or without a warning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An earlier source said the two groups did not avoid each other's pure items. If there were warnings, there is no problem. Without warnings, בית שמאי touching בית הלל's items is still fine, because anything בית הלל treats as pure is surely pure to בית שמאי. The real question is the other direction, which comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: They informed them, they let them know
They held back, they avoided
Items that are ritually impure
Items that are ritually pure
It makes sense, granted

phrases.english: Granted, if you say that they informed them,
phrases.notes: "They" means the two groups telling each other when an item was a problem in the other group's view.

phrases.english: that is why they did not hold back.
phrases.notes: They did not hold back from handling each other's pure items.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ דְּלָא מוֹדְעִי לְהוּ,
phrases.english: But if you say that they did not inform them,

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא בֵּית שַׁמַּאי מִבֵּית הִלֵּל לֹא נִמְנְעוּ —
phrases.english: granted, Beit Shammai did not hold back from Beit Hillel's items,
since the impure items of Beit Hillel
are pure items in Beit Shammai's view.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא דְּמוֹדְעִי לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a proof begun before this section about whether the two groups informed each other.
steps.raayaObject: That בית שמאי and בית הלל informed each other of problematic cases
steps.raayaSupportSource: The source saying they did not avoid each other's טהרות

steps.title: Why didn't בית הלל avoid בית שמאי's items? So they must have been told
steps.stepSummary: The other direction is a problem: things בית שמאי calls pure, בית הלל calls impure. So בית הלל could only use them safely if בית שמאי told them which items were a problem. The גמרא concludes that they did tell each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why didn't בית הלל avoid בית שמאי's items? What בית שמאי calls pure, בית הלל calls impure! It must be that they told them. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof: בית הלל could safely use בית שמאי's items only because בית שמאי warned them, so the two groups did inform each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the stricter side is the one using the lenient side's items. Without a warning, בית הלל would have been touching items that are impure in their own view. Since they did not hold back, there must have been warnings, and the גמרא accepts this with שמע מינה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not that... (leads to the forced conclusion)
Learn from this; the proof is accepted
Why

steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי and בית הלל did not simply ignore each other. When something was a problem in the other group's view, they told them.

phrases.english: But Beit Hillel from Beit Shammai's items,
why didn't they hold back?
The pure items of Beit Shammai
are impure items in Beit Hillel's view!
Rather, is it not that they informed them?
Learn from this.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בֵּית הִלֵּל מִבֵּית שַׁמַּאי לָמָּה לֹא נִמְנְעוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof by checking the direction that only works if there was a warning.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The two groups informed each other, as the purity case proves.

steps.title: What does the purity proof add beyond the marriage case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why this proof from purity is stronger than, or adds anything to, the earlier case about marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what makes this one stronger than that one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why it needed the purity case at all, since the same idea of telling each other was already raised about marriage. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both cases rest on the same idea: the groups told each other. So the purity proof seems to add nothing new. The גמרא wants to know what it teaches that the marriage case could not.

keyTerms.meaning: Its strength; what makes it stronger
This one compared to that one

phrases.english: And what makes this one stronger than that one?
phrases.notes: "This one" is the purity case; "that one" is the earlier case about marrying each other's families.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי אוּלְמֵיהּ דְּהָךְ מֵהָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the proof from step 2 was needed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new point the purity source adds beyond the marriage case

steps.title: A צרה marriage is well known, so we might have thought no warning was needed
steps.stepSummary: One might have said that a marriage involving a צרה is public knowledge anyway, so no special warning would be given. The purity proof shows that telling each other really was their practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that a צרה has publicity. So it teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question: the marriage case alone might be explained by the fact that everyone already knows about a צרה, so the purity proof was needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In marriage, one could think there was no need for a warning because a צרה marriage gets talked about on its own. Items of טהרה do not get that kind of attention, so the groups' behavior there shows that informing each other was a real practice.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken thought)
A co-wife, another wife of the same husband
It has publicity; people talk about it
It teaches us (that the first thought is wrong)

phrases.english: You might have said
that a rival wife has publicity,
so it teaches us.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא צָרָה קָלָא אִית לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: We might have thought a צרה marriage is well known and needs no warning. The proof shows that warning each other was their real practice.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: a ממזר comes only from ערוה with כרת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to רבי אלעזר's statement itself: although בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about צרות, both agree that a ממזר is born only from a union that is an איסור ערוה punishable by כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the main point. רבי אלעזר said: even though בית שמאי and בית הלל argued about צרות, they agree that a ממזר comes only from a union whose prohibition is an איסור ערוה punishable by כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: Using the word גופא, the גמרא opens a new discussion of רבי אלעזר's statement, which had been mentioned earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument about צרות could seem to create ממזרים in one group's eyes. רבי אלעזר says both groups agree on the rule for what makes a ממזר: only a union of ערוה with כרת, not a simple לאו.

keyTerms.meaning: Back to the statement itself, to discuss it directly
They agree, they concede
A child from a forbidden union who may not marry into the regular community
A forbidden relationship of the עריות category
Being cut off, a heavenly punishment

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the line for ממזרות: only a union of ערוה with כרת produces a ממזר, not a union forbidden by a simple לאו.

phrases.english: Returning to the matter itself, Rabbi Elazar said:
Even though they argued,
Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel, about rival wives,
they agree that there is no mamzer
except from one whose prohibition is a prohibition of forbidden relations
and is punishable by karet.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion of רבי אלעזר's statement, mentioned earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both בית שמאי and בית הלל agree that a ממזר comes only from a union of ערוה punishable by כרת.

steps.title: Who agrees with whom?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which side's agreement רבי אלעזר is talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who agrees?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who is agreeing to whom in רבי אלעזר's statement. This sets up a check of each possibility.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מודים means one side gives in to the other. The גמרא wants to know which side's agreement adds something real, and will test each option.

keyTerms.meaning: Who

phrases.english: Who agrees?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן מוֹדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for clarification of the word מודים in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which group is giving in to the other in רבי אלעזר's statement

steps.title: If בית שמאי agree with בית הלל, that is obvious
steps.stepSummary: If it means בית שמאי agree regarding cases done according to בית הלל, there is nothing new. In בית שמאי's view such a union is only a לאו, and children from a לאו are כשרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say בית שמאי agree to בית הלל, that is obvious! Children of people who break only a לאו are kosher!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first option and rejects it as too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a צרה marries someone else following בית הלל, in בית שמאי's view she has only broken a לאו. Everyone knows a לאו does not produce a ממזר, so רבי אלעזר would not need to tell us that בית שמאי agree to it.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces an option to be tested)
It is obvious, so why say it?
Those who are guilty only of breaking a לאו
Kosher; fit to marry normally

steps.confusionAlert: Here "agree to בית הלל" means agreeing about marriages done the way בית הלל rule. It does not mean בית שמאי changed their own view about צרות.

phrases.english: If we say Beit Shammai agree to Beit Hillel,
that is obvious!
Children of those liable for regular prohibitions
are fit!
phrases.notes: In בית שמאי's view, a צרה who married someone else without חליצה broke only a לאו.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא בֵּית שַׁמַּאי לְבֵית הִלֵּל פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to step 6 and rejects it.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading רבי אלעזר as "בית שמאי agree to בית הלל"
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In בית שמאי's view such a union is only a לאו, and everyone knows children of a לאו are כשרים, so the statement would teach nothing new.

steps.title: The other reading also fails: for בית הלל the case is כרת
steps.stepSummary: The other way to read 'they agree' is that בית הלל agree with בית שמאי, meaning the child of a צרה who did יבום according to בית שמאי is not a ממזר. That is impossible, because for בית הלל the צרה herself is forbidden with כרת, so her child is a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, perhaps it means בית הלל agree with בית שמאי. But for בית הלל, she herself is a case of those liable to כרת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the second way to read רבי אלעזר's 'both agree' and shows it does not work either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 7, 'בית שמאי agree with בית הלל' looked pointless, because for בית שמאי the union is only a לאו. The opposite reading fails for a different reason. It would mean בית הלל give in and say the child of a צרה who did יבום following בית שמאי is not a ממזר. But for בית הלל she is forbidden just like the ערוה, which carries כרת, so in their view her child must be a ממזר. The first reading seems to add nothing, and the second seems impossible.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, then (introduces the other option)
she herself
those whose forbidden union is punished with כרת

phrases.english: Rather, perhaps Beit Hillel agree with Beit Shammai —
but she herself is a case of those liable to karet!
phrases.notes: For בית הלל the צרה is forbidden just like the ערוה, so they could never agree that her child is not a ממזר.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בֵּית הִלֵּל לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided challenge begun in step 7 by rejecting the second possible reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of רבי אלעזר as 'בית הלל agree with בית שמאי'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In בית הלל's view the צרה is already חייבי כריתות, so her child is a ממזר. בית הלל could not concede otherwise, so this reading is impossible.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's point is to reject רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The reading really is 'בית שמאי agree with בית הלל.' The new point is that, against רבי עקיבא, a union forbidden only by a לאו does not produce a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it means בית שמאי agree with בית הלל. The statement comes to exclude the view of רבי עקיבא, who said a ממזר can come from a union forbidden by a לאו. It teaches us that a ממזר does not come from a union forbidden only by a לאו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It goes back to the first reading and explains what new thing it teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 objected that the first reading teaches nothing new. The answer is that it does teach something: it rules against רבי עקיבא. רבי עקיבא holds that a child from a union forbidden only by a לאו is a ממזר. רבי אלעזר is telling us that both בית שמאי and בית הלל reject that view, so only כרת unions produce a ממזר.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (sticks with the first option)
to exclude, to reject another opinion
unions forbidden by a plain prohibition (a לאו), not by כרת
it teaches us

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אלעזר, both בית שמאי and בית הלל agree that only a union punishable by כרת produces a ממזר. This is against רבי עקיבא, who says a union forbidden by a לאו can also produce one.
steps.confusionAlert: The new point here is not about צרות at all. It is about the general rule of when a child is a ממזר, and it rejects רבי עקיבא's opinion.
steps.whyThisMatters: This clarifies the basic rule of ממזרות: it requires an איסור כרת, not just a לאו.

phrases.english: Actually, Beit Shammai agree with Beit Hillel,
and it comes to exclude the view of Rabbi Akiva,
who said: there is a mamzer from unions liable for a prohibition,
it teaches us
that there is no mamzer from unions liable for a prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם בֵּית שַׁמַּאי לְבֵית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of steps 7 and 8 by returning to the first reading and naming its new point.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the statement's point is to reject another opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might have thought, like רבי עקיבא, that a union forbidden by a לאו also produces a ממזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both בית שמאי and בית הלל hold that only a כרת union produces a ממזר.

steps.title: A new proof begins: a ברייתא listing the disputes of בית שמאי and בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that starts by listing topics on which בית שמאי and בית הלל disagreed: צרות, sisters, an old גט, a doubtful married woman, and a divorced woman who stayed with her husband at an inn.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: Even though בית שמאי and בית הלל disagreed about rival wives and sisters, about an old גט, about a doubtful married woman, and about one who divorces his wife and she then lodges with him at an inn...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new proof about whether בית שמאי acted on their own view. It starts quoting a ברייתא, and this part only sets up the list. The punchline comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This goes back to the main question of whether בית שמאי actually acted on their opinion. The ברייתא first lists several areas where the two schools disagreed about marriage and divorce. These are areas where one school might call a child a ממזר or a woman a married woman when the other school would not. The 'even though' tells us a surprising conclusion about how they behaved is coming.

keyTerms.meaning: sisters, here two sisters who fall to יבום together
an 'old' גט: written, but the couple stayed together afterward
a woman whose status as a married woman is in doubt
an inn

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Although they disagreed —
Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel —
about rival wives and about sisters,
about an old bill of divorce,
phrases.notes: The husband wrote the גט but kept living with his wife. Can he still use that same גט later?

phrases.english: and about a doubtful married woman,
and about one who divorces his wife
and she lodged with him at an inn,

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנֶּחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the side discussion on רבי אלעזר, the גמרא returns to the main question with a new proof.
steps.raayaObject: Whether בית שמאי acted on their own opinion, and how the two schools related to each other's marriages
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing the topics on which בית שמאי and בית הלל disagreed (its conclusion comes in step 11)

steps.title: Despite their disputes, the two schools still married each other
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends its list with the dispute over the minimum value for קידושין. It then says that בית שמאי and בית הלל still married into each other's families, out of love and friendship.
steps.simpleTranslation: They also disagreed about קידושין done with money or something worth money, with a פרוטה or something worth a פרוטה. Even so, בית שמאי did not hold back from marrying women from בית הלל, and בית הלל did not hold back from marrying women from בית שמאי. This teaches you that they treated each other with affection and friendship, to fulfill the פסוק: 'Love truth and peace.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from step 10 finishes its list of disputes. It then says that these disputes did not stop the two schools from marrying each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every topic on the list affects whether a woman is married or whether her children may marry into the community. You would expect the two schools to stop marrying each other, but the ברייתא says they did not. Their love and friendship were stronger than their halachic disagreements.

keyTerms.meaning: Something worth money: an object used in place of coins
The smallest coin; for בית הלל it is enough for קידושין
They held back, they refrained
Affection and friendship

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic source showing that deep halachic disagreement does not have to break family and community ties.

phrases.english: By money and by something worth money,
by a פרוטה and by something worth a פרוטה —
בית שמאי did not hold back
from marrying women from בית הלל,
nor did בית הלל from בית שמאי.
This teaches you that affection and friendship
were practiced between them,
to fulfill what is said:
"Love truth and peace."

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא נִמְנְעוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי מִלִּישָּׂא נָשִׁים מִבֵּית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the list of disputes begun in step 10 and gives the ברייתא's main statement.
steps.raayaObject: Whether בית שמאי actually acted on their view about צרות
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about the two schools marrying each other

steps.title: רבי שמעון: they held back only in certain cases
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says the two schools did hold back from marrying in cases they knew for sure, but not in doubtful cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: They did hold back in the certain cases, but they did not hold back in the doubtful cases.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון, inside the same ברייתא, adds a limit to what was just said. They did refrain when they knew for sure that someone came from a disputed case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part of the ברייתא made it sound like there was no refraining at all. רבי שמעון says there was refraining when it was certain, and the next step will build a proof on this.

keyTerms.meaning: Certain, known for sure
Doubtful, not known

phrases.english: רבי שמעון says:
They did hold back from the certain cases,
but they did not hold back from the doubtful cases.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: נִמְנְעוּ הֵן מִן הַוַּדַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ברייתא's statement that they did not hold back.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In certain cases they refrained from marrying; in doubtful cases they did not.

steps.title: Holding back proves בית שמאי acted on their view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reasons: if they held back in certain cases, there must have been real cases where בית שמאי acted on their view.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense if you say they acted on their view; that is why they held back. But if you say they did not act on their view, why did they hold back?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses רבי שמעון's words to prove that בית שמאי really did act on their own view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If בית שמאי never acted differently from בית הלל, there would be nothing to avoid. Since רבי שמעון says they held back in certain cases, there must have been real marriages done according to בית שמאי.

keyTerms.meaning: They acted, they actually practiced their view
It makes sense if you say

phrases.english: It makes sense if you say they acted —
phrases.notes: "They" is בית שמאי; the open question is whether they actually practiced their view.

phrases.english: that is why they held back.
But if you say they did not act,
why did they hold back?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא עָשׂוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the proof out of רבי שמעון's statement.
steps.raayaObject: That בית שמאי acted on their view
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי שמעון's statement that they held back in certain cases

steps.title: Even if they acted, only בית הלל's holding back makes sense
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: even if בית שמאי acted, it is clear why בית הלל would hold back, because for them those unions carry כרת and the children are ממזרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really think so? Even granting that they acted, it makes sense that בית הלל held back from בית שמאי, because those unions are punishable by כרת, and the children are ממזרים according to בית הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to question the proof. This step only covers the side that makes sense; the real problem comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For בית הלל, a צרה who married the יבם according to בית שמאי is forbidden with כרת, so her children are ממזרים. So בית הלל holding back is easy to understand. The question is the other direction.

keyTerms.meaning: Can you really think so? A pushback on what was just said
Even granting that
Unions punishable by כרת

phrases.english: Can you really think so?
Even granting that they acted,
it makes sense for בית הלל —
they held back from בית שמאי,
because those are unions punishable by כרת,
and the children are ממזרים according to בית הלל.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִסְבְּרָא? נְהִי נָמֵי דְּעָשׂוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a challenge to the proof in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof in step 13 that the holding back shows בית שמאי acted on their view
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Holding back makes sense only for בית הלל; the next step shows it does not fit בית שמאי.

steps.title: Why would בית שמאי hold back, if the children are כשרים?
steps.stepSummary: For בית שמאי, a union done according to בית הלל is at most a לאו, and children of a לאו are כשרים. So why would בית שמאי hold back?
steps.simpleTranslation: But בית שמאי, why did they hold back from בית הלל? They are children of a union forbidden by a לאו, and such children are כשרים!
steps.whatsHappening: Here is the real problem. The ברייתא says both sides held back, but there seems to be no reason for בית שמאי to do so.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 taught that, unlike רבי עקיבא, a union forbidden only by a לאו does not produce a ממזר. So for בית שמאי, the children from בית הלל's cases are fully כשרים, and there is nothing to avoid.

keyTerms.meaning: Unions forbidden by a regular לאו, without כרת
Fit, allowed to marry into the community

phrases.english: But בית שמאי —
why did they hold back from בית הלל?
They are children of a union forbidden by a לאו,
and such children are כשרים!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בֵּית שַׁמַּאי — אַמַּאי נִמְנְעוּ מִבֵּית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge begun in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that both schools held back in certain cases
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Children of a union forbidden by a לאו are כשרים, so בית שמאי had no reason to avoid them.

steps.title: The holding back was about the צרה herself
steps.stepSummary: Using רב נחמן בר יצחק's words, the גמרא answers that בית שמאי held back from marrying the צרה herself, not her children.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב נחמן בר יצחק said: it was needed only for the צרה herself. Here too: it was needed only for the צרה herself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by borrowing a line from רב נחמן בר יצחק. The holding back was about marrying the צרה, not her children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed that 'holding back' meant avoiding the children. The answer changes that: בית שמאי avoided marrying the צרה herself, whose status they disagreed about. So the children being כשרים is no problem, and the proof that בית שמאי acted still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed only for: this teaching is about a narrower case
The צרה herself, not her children
Here too

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון's 'they held back in certain cases' shows that בית שמאי did act on their view. For בית שמאי, the holding back was about marrying the צרה herself, since her children would be כשרים anyway.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'held back' as meaning avoiding the children in both directions. For בית שמאי it means avoiding the צרה herself.

phrases.english: As רב נחמן בר יצחק said:
It was needed only for the צרה herself,
here too:
it was needed only for the צרה herself.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לַצָּרָה עַצְמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the holding back refers to the צרה herself, not her children.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Holding back meant avoiding the children, which would make no sense for בית שמאי.
steps.terutzMaskana: בית שמאי held back from marrying the צרה herself, so the proof that they acted on their view stands.

steps.title: A doubtful case is also forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי שמעון says they held back only in certain cases and not in doubtful ones, since a doubtful prohibition is still a prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between a certain case and a doubtful case? A certain case is forbidden, but a doubtful case is also forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון's statement from step 12. If they held back in certain cases, why didn't they also hold back in doubtful ones?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון split cases into וַדַּאי (they held back) and סָפֵק (they did not). The גמרא argues that a ספק of an איסור is still treated as an איסור. So the split seems to make no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: certain, a case known for sure
doubt, a case that is not clear
a prohibition, something forbidden
what is the difference?

phrases.english: And what is different from the certain case
that it is forbidden?
A doubtful case is also forbidden!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי שְׁנָא מִן הַוַּדַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side discussion in steps 13-16, the גמרא returns to examine the wording of רבי שמעון's statement in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's distinction between certain cases and doubtful cases
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A doubtful prohibition is still a prohibition, so they should have held back in doubtful cases too.

steps.title: Read it as 'unspecified', not 'doubtful'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads רבי שמעון's word: not 'doubtful' but 'unspecified', meaning a plain case where nobody raised any problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't say 'from the doubtful case.' Say 'from the unspecified case,' because they would tell each other about a problem, and then the others would hold back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by changing how we read רבי שמעון. He was talking about ordinary cases where no problem was mentioned, not real doubts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The families would warn each other whenever a marriage was forbidden according to their view. So if nobody said anything in a סְתָם case, that silence showed there was no problem. Real doubts would be avoided too, but those were not the cases רבי שמעון meant.

keyTerms.meaning: plain or unspecified, a case with no special information
they inform or notify
they separate, they hold back
don't say this, rather say that (rereading a text)

phrases.english: Do not say: from the doubtful case
Rather say: from the unspecified case
phrases.notes: An 'unspecified' case is an ordinary one where nobody raised any concern at all.

phrases.english: because they would inform them, and they would hold back

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תֵּימָא: מִן הַסָּפֵק, אֶלָּא אֵימָא: מִן הַסְּתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון meant that they did not hold back in real doubtful cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: He meant plain cases with no warning. Since the families always warned each other, silence meant the marriage was fine.

steps.title: Isn't this the same as the first part?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי שמעון adds. The idea that the schools trusted each other with love and friendship was already said at the start of the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us? That they treated each other with love and friendship? That is the same as the first part!
steps.whatsHappening: Now that רבי שמעון's words are reread, the גמרא asks what new point he is making.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the new reading, רבי שמעון's point is that the schools warned and trusted each other. But the opening of the ברייתא already said they acted with אהבה וריעות toward each other. So his statement seems to repeat it.

keyTerms.meaning: what is he teaching us? (what is new here?)
love and friendship
the first part (of the ברייתא)

phrases.english: And what is he teaching us
that they practiced love and friendship with each other?
That is the same as the first part!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading given in step 18, arguing that it makes רבי שמעון's statement say nothing new.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's statement as reread in step 18
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If it only teaches that the schools trusted each other, it repeats the first part of the ברייתא.

steps.title: The whole ברייתא is רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the point is not a new law. It teaches that the entire ברייתא, including the first part, was said by רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he teaches us: that the whole ברייתא is רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the repetition is fine. It shows that the whole ברייתא comes from one תנא, רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might have thought רבי שמעון was arguing with the first part of the ברייתא. The answer says he is not arguing; he is explaining it. So the first part and his words form one consistent teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: this is what he teaches us
all of it, the whole thing

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון's words do not argue with the start of the ברייתא. The whole ברייתא is his: the schools warned each other, so in plain cases with no warning they married freely.

phrases.english: This is what he teaches us
that the whole of it is רבי שמעון

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דְּכוּלַּהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying who said the source (one תנא for the whole ברייתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון's statement repeats the first part for no reason, or argues with it.
steps.terutzMaskana: His statement shows that the first part is also his, so the ברייתא is one unified teaching.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן בן נורי: a problem either way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a new source. רבי יוחנן בן נורי asks how the law of צרות should be practiced, since each school's practice creates a problem for the other, and he starts to propose an enactment.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יוחנן בן נורי said, how should this law spread among the Jewish people? If we act like בית שמאי, the child is a ממזר according to בית הלל. If we act like בית הלל, the child is flawed according to בית שמאי. Come, let us make an enactment for the צרות...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new proof for the open question of what was done in practice. This step sets up the source; the גמרא's actual inference from it comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each path has a cost. Following בית שמאי produces a ממזר according to בית הלל. Following בית הלל produces a child who is פגום, not a ממזר but with damaged status, according to בית שמאי. This echoes steps 14-15, where the children of a לאו union were called כשרים, meaning not ממזרים; here רבי יוחנן בן נורי adds that they are still פגום, and his wording 'how should we act' is what the גמרא will build on.

keyTerms.meaning: spreads, becomes widespread in practice
flawed, damaged in family status but not a ממזר
let us make an enactment, a rabbinic fix
co-wives, the other wives of the man who died

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up ממזר and פגום. A ממזר comes from a union that carries כרת. A פגום child comes from a union that is only a לאו, so he is not a ממזר, but his status is still damaged.

phrases.english: Come and hear
for רבי יוחנן בן נורי said
How will this law become widespread among Israel?
phrases.notes: 'This law' means the law of צרות that the two schools argue about.

phrases.english: If we act according to בית שמאי
the child is a ממזר according to בית הלל
If we act according to בית הלל
the child is flawed according to בית שמאי
Come, let us make an enactment for the co-wives

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the explanation of רבי שמעון, the גמרא brings a new source about whether the schools acted on their views in practice.
steps.raayaObject: Whether בית שמאי actually acted on their view about צרות
steps.raayaSupportSource: The statement of רבי יוחנן בן נורי describing the problem with each practice and proposing an enactment for the צרות
